detections.evidence_quote: this whole scholarship thing was an excuse to bring. Foreign doctors into the United States because all the American doctors were in Vietnam, and there was a big shortage of physicians.
detections.summary: Guest describes coming to the US on a scholarship he says was a pretext to import foreign doctors during a Vietnam-era physician shortage, working in a community hospital as cheap labor.

detections.evidence_quote: So we had gunshot wounds.
detections.summary: Guest recalls treating gunshot wounds in a traumatic community-hospital environment.

detections.evidence_quote: I then took specialty training in endocrinology, which is the study of hormones, and then in neuroendocrinology, which is looking at brain chemistry.
detections.summary: Guest outlines his medical training: internal medicine residency at a Harvard-affiliated institution, then endocrinology and neuroendocrinology.

detections.evidence_quote: still smoking and drinking and partying as a. Intern and resident
detections.summary: Guest notes he was still smoking, drinking and partying as an intern and resident.

detections.evidence_quote: We were discovering in the brain these chemicals that now everybody knows about. They're called neuropeptides.
detections.summary: Guest recounts the 1970s discovery of brain neuropeptides and Candace Pert's phrase 'molecules of emotion', naming serotonin, dopamine, oxytocin and opiates.

detections.evidence_quote: Got me hooked to the so-called mind-body connection
detections.summary: Guest says the 'molecules of emotion' drew him to the mind-body connection, puzzled why patients with the same illness and treatment had different outcomes, and began recording their stories.

detections.evidence_quote: I was also seeing patients, and I was very perplexed as to why two patients who had the same illness could see the same doctor
detections.summary: Guest's observations of his own patients' divergent outcomes are offered as the grounds for his interest in mind-body effects.

detections.evidence_quote: I then started submitting these to medical journals, but nobody would accept them.
detections.summary: Medical journals rejected his patient stories as too anecdotal with not enough research, and publishers found them too New Age.

detections.evidence_quote: they're too anecdotal. There's not enough research.
detections.summary: Journals' stated reason for rejection: the patient stories were too anecdotal and lacked research.

detections.evidence_quote: I had given up alcohol and I had given up every experiment. I was meditating
detections.summary: Guest says he gave up alcohol and his experiments and took up meditation.
